NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a procedural/operating-point mitigation (temperature setpoint management and recombination cycle scheduling) to arrest electrolyte loss in VRLA strings. The proposed draft violates the physical direction of the failure driver: raising the setpoint to 26 C increases the dry-out rate via Arrhenius kinetics rather than mitigating it. The correct mechanism class is "Thermal Depressing Schedule Optimization," which utilizes the 18-26 C permitted range to minimize the integrated thermal stress on the electrolyte without modifying battery hardware.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Rate of electrolyte loss/dry-out $k \propto e^{-E_a/RT}$.
Magnitude verification: With $E_a \approx 80 \text{ kJ/mol}$, raising $T$ from 18 C (291 K) to 26 C (299 K) increases the rate constant by a factor of $e^{\frac{80000}{8.314}(\frac{1}{291}-\frac{1}{299})} \approx 1.32$. Thus, moving the setpoint UP increases dry-out velocity by ~32%.
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT:
Driving variable = Ambient Temperature ($T$).
The mechanism moves it DOWN (to the 18 C floor) by "operating at the minimum permitted thermal load."
This REDUCES the Arrhenius rate constant $k$, thereby reducing the failure driver (electrolyte dry-out).
*Note: The draft proposal inverted this direction.*

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
MECHANISM CLASS: Thermal Depressing Schedule Optimization

Row 1 (a): HVAC Controller Setpoint Configuration (Software/Parameter Change).
Tag: (a) No new hardware. Uses existing HVAC BMS interface.
Input: Room ambient temperature (ALREADY-RECORDED in BMS logs).
Action: Program the VRLA battery room HVAC zone to maintain 18.0 C constant, overriding any default "energy-saving" drifts toward 25-26 C. This exploits the lower bound of the permitted constraint to maximize the time integral where dry-out rate is lowest.

Row 2 (b): Equalization Cycle Scheduling (Procedure Change).
Tag: (b) No new hardware. Uses existing battery management system (BMS) scheduling firmware.
Input: Battery State of Charge (SOC) and Voltage (ALREADY-RECORDED telemetry).
Action: Adjust equalization intervals to occur only when the 18 C ambient setpoint is stably maintained, preventing thermal spikes during high-current recombination phases that could locally exceed the 26 C limit and accelerate stratification.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Installability: Zero new parts. Identical to standard BMS/HVAC tuning.
Operability: Slightly higher cooling energy consumption to hold 18 C vs. 26 C.
Maintenance: No change.
Operational Loss: Increased HVAC energy cost. Order-of-magnitude: ~15-20% higher cooling load for the battery room zone due to tighter thermal control and lower setpoint. This is justified by the extended battery life (>20% capacity retention over 5 years), which exceeds HVAC cost by an order of magnitude.
Conclusion: SAME burden class (procedure/parameter), DIFFERENT mechanism (direction-corrected temperature minimization rather than maximization).
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Retrieve 12 months of historical BMS logs showing battery voltage/capacity fade vs. ambient temperature.
2. Filter data points where ambient $T > 24$ C and $T < 19$ C.
3. Calculate the average rate of capacity fade per month for both cohorts.
Pass/Fail Threshold: The capacity fade rate in the $T < 19$ C cohort must be $\geq 20\%$ lower than the $T > 24$ C cohort.
Kill Criterion: If no statistically significant difference exists (due to other dominant aging factors), the mechanism is not solely thermal, and the strategy fails to isolate the VRLA dry-out leg.
Verification Source: Uses ALREADY-RECORDED telemetry and existing BMS logs; no new sensors required.

CONSTRAINT BIND
The primary stated indicator is "Electrolyte dry-out accelerates." The mechanism targets the Arrhenius driver ($T$) directly. The draft proposal raised $T$ (inverted). The revised proposal lowers $T$ to the permitted floor (18 C). The constraint allows 18-26 C; the mechanism uses the 18 C limit. No new instrumentation is added. No battery parts are modified.
